text:
carmen: Heads up — planning a 6-week writing retreat in Lisbon (May 4–Jun 14). I will be working full-time from there. Quick q: does the WFH stipend continue / get pro-rated? Any payroll/tax paperwork I should file before I go? Also worried about benefits/social security. TIA
matt: cc'ing people-ops. Approving the time — +1 from me, Carmen. Please loop them in. :thumbsup:
elena: Hey Carmen — short answer: probably yes but we need a Temp Remote request and payroll notified. Steps: 1) submit the Temporary Remote form (https://intra.redwood/work-requests/temporary-remote) 2) add the dates to your Homebase travel record (do NOT change legal home base) 3) payroll will annotate your record for the period 4) confirm visa/entry rules. Stipend is pro-rated by days; default WFH stipend is $120/mo and we'll pro-rate in payroll. Benefits remain active for short travel. I'll loop in tax & legal to confirm SS/tax specifics.
carmen: Thanks — when you say "do NOT change legal home base" do you mean leave my country of record as US and only mark travel dates? Also is a tourist visa OK for 6 weeks?
elena: Correct — leave legal home base as US. Only add a temporary-remote entry with dates and purpose. For <=183 days we usually keep employees on US payroll; the 183-day rule is a common threshold for tax/residency but countries vary. Legal will confirm visa.
marcus: Legal here — for US passport holders, Schengen tourist entry for ~6 weeks is generally fine. Digital nomad visas are unnecessary for a short stay and usually have multi-month minimums. We recommend checking passport validity and any entry forms, but no change to employment contract needed.
nina: Tax team — Portugal specifics: under ~90 days you typically don't trigger Portuguese tax residency, but rules depend on facts (family, housing, local bank accounts). Social security typically stays with the US employer for short visits unless there's a local secondment or contract. If you have any paid work for a Portuguese business or local contractor arrangements, inform us. Please attach exact dates to the form so we can confirm no PE/tax nexus risk.
carmen: Got it — and the stipend pro-rate math?
elena: Example math: $120/month ÷ 30 * days remote in that month. If your trip spans two payroll periods we'll pro-rate across both. Default is pro-rate; if you want an exception (e.g., whole-month payout) mention it in the form and manager can approve, but not guaranteed.
carmen: Will my health insurance still cover me while in Portugal for six weeks?
elena: Benefits remain active for short foreign travel, yes. Check the Benefits Abroad FAQ (https://intra.redwood/benefits/faq#abroad) — some plans require pre-authorization for treatment overseas or have limited coverage for elective care. For emergency care most plans provide coverage but you may need to file claims upon return.
carmen: Filing form now, thanks.
payroll-bot: Temp Remote request received for carmen on 1800001122. Notifying Payroll & Tax teams to review. (automated message)
matt: Thanks — please @me once Payroll confirms the stipend pro-rate and that benefits are ok.
carmen: :thumbsup: will do
